Writing this from a throwaway since my employer knows my reddit username.

I'm 24. When I graduated I found out that most local companies have no idea on what they are doing. Most codebases I have seen are piles upon piles of spaghetti code. No automated testing. No continuous integration/delivery at all. No design patterns anywhere. Huge classes with a ton of static methods doing all the work. Deployments are a nightmare and done manually. Downtime due to deployments is a regular occurrence. Most companies follow a waterfall approach as well. Most of the "developers" working for these companies are hired without being interviewed first and most don't know the difference between an object and a class. People don't know of any languages other than C# and Java. I hope I drew a clear picture of the dismal state of software in the country I live in.

I have been working remotely for a US software consultancy working in a ton of different projects written in Ruby for a year or so. I bill US rates and they think I'm worth it. All of this top quality (fully tested, decoupled) production code to handle production websites that move millions of dollars per day.

I'm also a big participant in open source and have contributed to high profile projects in Haskell, Ruby and JavaScript. Meaningful contributions, not removing whitespace. I mostly code in Haskell in my spare time but I have also written a fair amount of production Haskell code. I have trained US developers by doing remote pair-programming. I have been working in English all the time as well. There are some kind of popular libraries in Hackage that are maintained by me.

The past week or so I realized I need to leave this country if I want to advance my career. I could keep working remotely, but career advancement is limited when working this way. I'm contacted fairly often by recruiters in the US and all of them think I'm from the US and back-off after I tell them I'm not in the US. I need to leave this country and leave it soon if I don't want my career to stagnate. I don't even know where these people find my email address since I don't maintain a LinkedIn or publish my email in GitHub.

I wish I could accept the jobs these recruiters offer, but I can't due to my citizenship. As I said I'm from a third world country and most countries (likely all) developed countries require visas for people from my country in order to enter. I'm single and have no obligations tying me to this country. Starting a company here is not an option since this is a very unstable country and doing so is very risky.

What are my options here? Apply for a H1B? Skilled migrants programs in NZ/Aus/Canada?

I could keep up with the remote work since it pays well, but my career is not going to advance this way, is it?
I live in a third world country with an extremely poor software industry, how do I advance my career?

[help] Performing unique actions on elements with the same identifiers?
Don't have elements with the same identifiers. It's bad.

Ok, so this might be slightly (4 months :P) late... (but just for completion, since I'd like voat to succeed, and am exceedingly pissed off with some other site at the moment)

1) As Etna says, you mustn't have two elements in your HTML that have the same ID. However, you don't have this problem in your code.

2) When an event handler is called, it gets passed an event object as its first argument, like so...

$something.on('click', function(event) {
});

3) This event object has lots of useful properties. For the click event, this includes event.target, which is the element that you clicked on. See MDN: Click event for more info.

4) So, in your event handler, you need to a) Get the element clicked upon b) Get that element's enclosing UL c) Find $first, $next, $selected inside that UL d) The rest of your code should work as is.

Hopefully working demo: http://codepen.io/anon/pen/rVKrEG
